frontmatter.title: Electronic energy estimation
frontmatter.description: A molecular Hamiltonian, explicit controlled evolution, retained-target QPE confidence and resource scaling.

children.value: Molecular energies appear as eigenphases of Hamiltonian evolution. Phase estimation converts those phases into measured bitstrings; state preparation determines which energy is likely to appear. A Hartree–Fock state can overlap strongly with a small molecule’s ground state, but that overlap is an input to the success calculation rather than a free guarantee

This chapter connects the classical Hamiltonian input, actual controlled gates, preparation, phase resolution, repeated measurements and classical decoding. It also makes a confidence distinction visible: the minimum of many raw QPE samples can select a low-energy tail outlier. Our protocol takes a median of repeated QPE rounds on the
, then the minimum across independently prepared groups.

A verified two-qubit H₂ fixture and explicit dimer evolution supply the first example. The fundamental repeated-access circuit, analytic-power variant and recycled-clock instrument are implemented and checked; a separate

constructs full four-qubit product-formula evolution. Large generated circuits and conditional physical projections have separate evidence labels. The example is deliberately coarse in energy resolution. Fresh SCF/mapping, general molecular state preparation, hardware initialization and certified synthesis remain outside the present physical estimate.

The task is the energy of a finite-basis Hamiltonian with nuclei fixed at the stated geometry. Basis/model errors are separate from quantum phase accuracy. The stored input is neutral H₂ at a separation of

Within a group, R odd QPE rounds use fresh clocks on the

. Their joint outcome law is a spectral mixture of conditional IID phase distributions. Repreparing HF every round would instead multiply mixed marginals and would invalidate this median contract. Fresh-clock measurements can be deferred until all rounds finish; the baseline is consequently a static circuit accepted by the current estimator.

contract = energy.ground_energy_contract(model, phase_bits=5, ideal_failure=.005)
R = contract["qpe_rounds_per_retained_target"]
K = contract["independent_groups"]
samples = energy.sample_retained_target_groups(model, phase_bits=5, rounds=R, groups=K, seed=20261112)
reference = energy.reference_spectral_law(model, phase_bits=5)
robust = energy.robust_energy_reference(model, phase_bits=5, rounds=R, groups=K)
error = abs(samples["estimate"] - reference["ground_energy"])
assert robust["ideal_success_within_grid_error"] >= contract["ideal_confidence_lower_bound"] - 1e-12
print("Groups / rounds:", K, R)
print("Ideal absolute energy tolerance (Ha):", contract["energy_absolute_error_ideal"])
print("Ideal confidence lower bound:", contract["ideal_confidence_lower_bound"])
print("Independent exact-law success:", robust["ideal_success_within_grid_error"])
print("Actual sequential gate/projection estimate (Ha):", samples["estimate"])
print("Reference error (Ha):", error)
print("Sequential simulation wires:", samples["simulated_width"], "; complete deferred register allocated:", samples["full_deferred_register_statevector_allocated"])
for group in samples["groups"]:
    print("Group", group["group"], "outcomes", group["outcomes"], "median", group["median_outcome"])

children.value: The physical estimate excludes fresh logical-zero initialization/reset cost, SCF/mapping, classical compilation and readout/communication latency.
QDK abstracts Clifford scheduling and supplies no concrete angle-synthesis sequence or output-error certificate. The

remain conditional models, with hardware energy-confidence fields false. They do not inherit a hardware success guarantee from the ideal median theorem or claim superiority over the different Grover task.

Independent checks compare the actual two-qubit gate access with SciPy matrix exponentiation, controlled powers with direct matrix powers including identity phase, complete small retained-target circuits with a spectral joint law, and reset instruments with the deferred static circuit. The fixture’s original four-qubit particle sector independently matches the stored reduced matrix. Additional random coefficients, complex states and multiple active dimers test signs, basis order and normalization.
The canonical default is sampled by a bounded
, preserving the target between rounds. This evaluates the output law of the deferred 97-wire circuit; it does not allocate a

statevector or validate arbitrary input-register semantics. Small complete 11-wire circuits are separately simulated. Dense references stop at eight data qubits, complete statevectors at 14 wires and sequential runs at 1,024 rounds.

No Lean formalization is integrated for these circuits. The ideal spectral-mixture/median reasoning and numerical tests do not certify compiled hardware. Proof artifacts would need an exact theorem, input domain, source correspondence and reproduced toolchain.
Recorded native computation and routine CI

children.label: Recorded native computation and routine CI

children.value: The six native energy resource records were computed in a separate bounded CPU job with Python 3.12.14 and the full environment lock. The complete producer finished in
, with two explicitly selected CPUs and peak resident memory
. This is classical estimation-process memory, separate from the modeled quantum space. The

binds the exact saved files, producer and verifier sources, environment, seed and successful completion evidence. Its native producer commit identifies the measured source snapshot; the published source has matching content hashes.

Routine CI runs the current producer with native resource estimation disabled in a fresh temporary directory. It reconstructs the logical circuits, bounded samples and classical checks, compares the QASM and logical evidence, authenticates the saved native records and independently checks their model arithmetic. It preserves the native factory choices and Pareto records; it does not repeat their search. Changed producer, lock, verifier or record bytes require a reviewed new freeze. The same physical exclusions and false synthesis/hardware-certificate flags apply to both the recorded computation and this replay.
The four single-round spectral-reference arrays admit a nominal absolute replay tolerance of

for floating-point differences between hosts. Their shapes, order, ranges, normalization and fixed-weight marginal relation are checked. For the fixed 11-wire test (one dimer, three phase bits and three rounds), each reported maximum joint-probability residual must satisfy the producer’s existing

bound. Sampled outcomes, weights, all remaining result fields, circuit exports, budgets and immutable file hashes retain exact comparisons. These numerical checks are separate from the quantum error allocations.
